The Movement of the Third and Fourth Derivatives of a Jeffreys Block

Source: R/jfp_move.R
jfp_mv_ctx.Rd

jfp_mv_ctx() sets up, for one block and up to two directions, the context from which jfp_mv_white(), jfp_mv_B() and jfp_mv_pair() compute the three objects of the third and fourth derivatives of \(\log|\tilde I|\): the whitened derivative of the block's matrix along the directions, the rows \(B_R\) of the low-rank terms, and the trace terms \(T_R(Y)_{kl} = \partial_R\,\mathrm{tr}(\tilde Y\,\partial_{kl} \tilde I)\) with \(\tilde Y = U^{-1}YU^{-\top}\).

Usage

jfp_mv_ctx(st, bs, ds)

jfp_mv_white(cx, R)

jfp_mv_B(cx, R)

jfp_mv_pair(cx, Y, R)

Arguments

st

A state, from jfp_state().

bs

A block's entry of the state.

ds

A named list of directions (v, and w for the fourth derivative), each from jfp_dir().

cx

A context, from jfp_mv_ctx().

R

A character vector naming the directions taken, a subset of names(ds).

Y

A symmetric \(\tilde p\times\tilde p\) matrix.

Value

jfp_mv_ctx() an environment; jfp_mv_white() a \(\tilde p\times\tilde p\) matrix; jfp_mv_B() a matrix over the joint vector and the \(\tilde p^2\) entries; jfp_mv_pair() a list with sparse (per-observation weights keyed as statmod_information_at() reads its H) and dense (a list of entries idx, X, each adding X in the rows idx and its transpose in the columns idx).

Details

With the block's rows in one equation, \(\tilde I = \sum_t w_tJ_t \tilde V_t^\top\tilde V_t\) with \(J_t\) the family's expected information of that equation. Each derivative distributes the directions over \(J\) and the two factors \(\tilde V\) by the Leibniz rule (jfp_leibniz()), and a derivative of \(J\) is the Faa di Bruno sum in the predictors, with the second derivative of a predictor where a term in its equation recomputes its block at the coefficients (jfp_mv_J()). A free index enters the information through the Jacobian column and through the derivative of the moving block along the directions, and it enters the rows only in the term that holds the block. For a model whose predictors are linear and a block whose rows do not move, every share beyond the design's cross products is zero and the objects are those of the static derivatives.

In a model with a filter the Jacobian columns are the joint rows of every equation (jfp_jac()), and each equation that the filter drives is a moving unit whose derivatives along the directions come from the filter's kernels (jfp_mv_rows()). A block in the subformula of a filter's parameter has rows in every equation that the filter drives, so \(\tilde I = \sum_t w_t\sum_{q,r}I_{qr,t}\tilde V_{q,t}^\top \tilde V_{r,t}\) and the three objects are summed over the ordered pairs \((q, r)\) (jfp_mv_setpair()); the rows' derivatives are read along the block's whitened directions \(d_i\), one kernel call per direction.
